OBJECTIVE: Mutations in KCNQ2 and KCNQ3, encoding the voltage-gated potassium channels KV 7.2 and KV 7.3, are known to cause benign familial neonatal seizures mainly by haploinsufficiency.

OBJECTIVE: Mutations in KCNQ2 and KCNQ3, encoding the voltage-gated potassium channels KV 7.2 and KV 7.3, are known to cause benign familial neonatal seizures mainly by haploinsufficiency.
We observed a clear loss of function for all mutations.

Strikingly, 5 of 7 mutations exhibited a drastic dominant-negative effect on wild-type KV 7.2 or KV 7.3 subunits, either by globally reducing current amplitudes (3 pore mutations) or by a depolarizing shift of the activation curve (2 voltage sensor mutations) decreasing potassium currents at the subthreshold level at which these channels are known to critically influence neuronal firing.

Strikingly, 5 of 7 mutations exhibited a drastic dominant-negative effect on wild-type KV 7.2 or KV 7.3 subunits, either by globally reducing current amplitudes (3 pore mutations) or by a depolarizing shift of the activation curve (2 voltage sensor mutations) decreasing potassium currents at the subthreshold level at which these channels are known to critically influence neuronal firing.
Application of retigabine, a recently marketed KV 7 channel opener, partially reversed these effects for the majority of analyzed mutations.

Here, we set out to determine the disease mechanism of 7 de novo missense KCNQ2 mutations that were recently described in patients with a severe epileptic encephalopathy including pharmacoresistant seizures and pronounced intellectual disability.
